title: Preserve authenticated recovery for long portfolio runs
description:
A long-running local portfolio dogfood attempt completed ranking and substantial assessment progress, then lost Plexus application authentication. The procedure failed before diagnosis, and required terminal task-output artifact persistence failed through the same unavailable authorization path. Published evidence must remain immutable, and a renewed session must resume safely rather than silently starting over.

Feature: Recover long portfolio runs after application-session expiry

Scenario: Authentication expires during analysis
  Given a portfolio run has published durable start and ranking evidence
  And assessment is still running
  When the application session becomes unavailable
  Then the run records an actionable authentication interruption when authority permits
  And it does not label the analysis complete
  And no optimization is launched

Scenario: Resume after renewed authentication
  Given a failed or interrupted attempt has immutable checkpoints and a frozen run identity
  When an operator renews the application session and resumes the procedure
  Then recovery verifies the exact Task, Report, Procedure, run specification, checkpoint, and evidence fingerprint
  And it continues only from authoritative durable evidence
  And it never silently duplicates already completed work or creates an unrelated successful attempt

Scenario: Terminal artifact persistence loses authorization
  Given procedure output persistence is required
  When artifact-ticket authorization is unavailable
  Then the request fails visibly without an inline fallback
  And previously published Report evidence remains available
  And the operator receives a concrete reauthentication and recovery next action

Sanitized observation: an exhaustive run stopped partway through assessment after application authentication became unavailable, and required task-output artifact persistence also failed. No client identity, score data, or opaque run identifiers are stored here.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Dogfood evidence recorded: the interrupted run had already published immutable start and ranking revisions and was partway through exhaustive assessment. Application authentication became unavailable; the procedure failed before semantic diagnosis, and the required terminal task-output attachment could not obtain an artifact ticket. No optimizer or protected mutation occurred. Next work must prove exact-checkpoint recovery after renewed authentication and preserve the failed attempt rather than relabeling it successful.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Read-only investigation: the observed interruption is a missing local application refresh credential, not a rejected refresh grant. The run had committed start/ranking evidence and live assessment progress, but partial assessment rows were not committed as an immutable checkpoint. Existing recovery is not an explicit authenticated-portfolio recovery contract; implementation must preserve the active attempt, verify its frozen identity and committed revision after reauthentication, and resume only the unfinished deterministic work. Separate the primary authentication interruption from the secondary required-output artifact publication failure in operator-facing evidence. No client-specific information recorded.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Increment 1A started: add outside-in auth-layer specifications for missing credential, confirmed invalid/revoked refresh, and transient refresh transport failure. Scope is limited to cognito.py and its focused tests; portfolio and recovery code remain untouched.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Increment 1A red/green evidence: added focused outside-in specifications. Red: collection failed because the new typed auth outcomes were not implemented. Green: focused auth suite passes (24 tests) after the minimal auth-layer change; static style check passes and git diff --check is clean. Behavior now distinguishes absent local refresh credential, explicit OAuth invalid_grant, and unproven refresh transport failure. Only explicit invalid_grant clears the keychain credential; a transient failure preserves it and a subsequent refresh succeeds. Portfolio/checkpoint code was not changed.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Increment 1A review follow-up, red-first: a regression using a real HTTP 400 response showed that response truthiness discarded the explicit invalid_grant evidence when the HTTP client raised directly. The auth layer now selects the attached response by explicit presence. New contracts cover direct invalid_grant rejection, 5xx, malformed error content, other OAuth 400 errors, typed base compatibility, and exception chaining. Refresh-focused set passes 27 tests; style and scoped diff checks pass. The two fixed-port loopback tests await release of an unrelated active interactive login listener before the complete file is rerun.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Increment 1A review follow-up is fully green after the interactive callback listener exited: complete auth suite 29 passed; scoped flake8 and git diff --check passed. The explicit invalid_grant path deletes the credential and preserves the HTTP error as its cause; 5xx, malformed/non-JSON content, non-invalid_grant 400 responses, and timeouts retain the credential and raise a typed transient failure with exception chaining. No portfolio or recovery code changed.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Increment 1B started. Scope is an optimization-portfolio-only authority preflight before any stakeholder-visible Task, Report, or procedure claim. It will reuse the existing Cognito auth service and typed outcomes; no credential serialization, resources, or ordinary-command behavior changes. Outside-in specs will demonstrate no mutation on missing, rejected, or transient authority.

comments.author: ryan.porter
ryan.porter
comments.text: Increment 1B runtime preflight is implemented and at a coherent tested point. The default stateful portfolio execution path obtains an access token through CognitoAuthService before it constructs a dashboard client or reads/creates Task, Report, or ChatMessage state. Missing session, confirmed refresh rejection, and transient refresh failure propagate as their existing typed actionable outcomes. Outside-in contracts demonstrate no client/account/stakeholder mutation for each outcome, successful token acquisition precedes client construction, and read-only ranking does not invoke this portfolio-only preflight. Focused runtime set: 5 passed. Complete runtime suite: 273 passed. git diff --check passed. No credentials are serialized and no resources/schema are changed. Paused after this coherent point for the active production snapshot/launch.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Production dogfooding of Increment 1B confirmed a remaining boundary: the YAML CLI path creates the outer Procedure, Task, and TaskStages before the Tactus runtime invokes the portfolio-specific application-authority preflight. The preflight still protects Report creation and portfolio work, but it does not yet satisfy the stricter scenario that missing authority causes zero stakeholder-state mutation. Follow-up must move or duplicate the typed authority check into the procedure CLI/service path before create-or-claim, with outside-in proof that no Procedure/Task is created when authority is unavailable.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Reproduced the post-login rough edge as a transient OAuth refresh transport failure with the durable credential intact. Added a bounded automatic retry policy: up to three total token attempts with 0.2s and 0.5s delays; only explicit invalid_grant deletes the credential and it is never retried. Failing-first retry specs now pass. Focused auth/CLI validation: 33 passed; diff check clean; three fresh live whoami processes all succeeded.
